textbookText: 2. HNO3 as an oxidizing agent

Nitric acid is a strong oxidizing agent because in HNO3 the oxidation state of N is +5 which is highest. The oxidation state of N in HNO3 can only be decreased so it acts as an oxidizing agent and oxidizes many metals, metalloids, non-metals and other inorganic compounds etc.
Some oxidizing reactions of nitric acid are:

A. Oxidation of metals Several metals except inert metals like Pt, Au, Ir, etc. react with nitric acid under different conditions to produce nitrate salts, water, oxides of nitrogen. The nature of the products depends upon the following three main factors:
a. The nature of the metals b. The concentration of nitric acid and c. The temperature The mode of reaction between nitric acid and metals can be categorized as
Action with more electropositive metals Metals which are more electropositive (like Mg, Mn, Zn, Fe, etc.) than hydrogen react with nitric acid according to nascent hydrogen theory.

Metal + HNO3 → Metal nitrate + [H] HNO3 + [H] → Reduction product + Water Some examplesa. Action on Zinc: Zinc reacts with nitric acid under various conditions to produce different products as explained belowWith hot and conc. HNO3: Zn reacts with hot and conc. HNO3 to give nitrogen dioxide along with zinc nitrate and water.

Zn + 2HNO3 → Zn(NO3)2 +2[H] {HNO3 + [H] → NO2 + H2O }× 2 Zn + 4HNO3 → Zn(NO3)2 + 2NO2 + 2H2O With hot and moderately conc. HNO3: Zn reacts with hot and moderately conc. HNO3 to give nitric oxide along with zinc nitrate and water. {Zn + 2HNO3 → Zn(NO3)2 +2[H]}×3 {HNO3 + [H] → NO+ 2H2O }× 2 3Zn + 8HNO3 → 3Zn(NO3)2 + 2NO + 4H2O With cold and dil. HNO3: Zn reacts with cold and dil. HNO3 to give nitrous oxide along with zinc nitrate and water. {Zn + 2HNO3 → Zn(NO3)2 +2[H]}×4 2HNO3 + 8[H] → N2O + 5H2O 4Zn + 10HNO3 → 4Zn(NO3)2 + N2O + 5H2O

With very dil. HNO3: Zn reacts very dil. HNO3 to give ammonium nitrate along with zinc nitrate and water. {Zn + 2HNO3 → Zn(NO3)2 +2[H]}×4 HNO3 + 8[H] → NH3 + 3H2O NH3 + HNO3 → NH4NO3 4Zn + 10HNO3 → 4Zn(NO3)2 + NH4NO3 + 3H2O

b. Action on Magnesium: The reaction of Mg with conc. and moderately conc. nitric acid are same as that of zinc. With hot and conc. HNO3: Mg reacts with hot and conc. HNO3 to give nitrogen dioxide along with magnesium nitrate and water.

Mg + 2HNO3 → Mg(NO3)2 +2[H] {HNO3 + [H] → NO2 + H2O }× 2 Mg + 4HNO3 → Mg(NO3)2 + 2NO2 + 2H2O With hot and moderately conc. HNO3: Mg reacts with hot and moderately conc. HNO3 to give nitric oxide along with magnesium nitrate and water. {Mg + 2HNO3 → Mg(NO3)2 +2[H]}×3 {HNO3 + [H] → NO+ 2H2O }× 2 3Mg + 8HNO3 → 3Mg(NO3)2 + 2NO + 4H2O But, Mg reacts with very dilute nitric acid to produce magnesium nitrate and hydrogen gas. Mg + 2HNO3 → Mg(NO3)2 + H2 ↑ Note: These above reactions can also be balanced by producing nascent oxygen instead of nascent hydrogen.
c. Action on Iron: Iron reacts with nitric acid under various conditions to produce different products as explained below-

With hot and conc. HNO3: When iron reacts with heat and conc. HNO3, a layer of iron oxide (Fe3O4) is formed on the surface of it which stops the reaction. This is called passivation or passivity of iron and such iron is called passive iron.
HNO3 → H2O + 2NO2 + [O]}×4 3Fe + 4[O] → Fe3O4 3Fe+ 8HNO3 → Fe3O4 + 8NO2 + 4H2O Hence, Fe + HNO3 → No reaction (Hot & Conc.)
Facts Similar behavior is shown by other metals like Al, Cr, Co and Ni.

With hot and moderately conc. HNO3: Iron reacts with moderately conc. HNO3 to give nitrogen dioxide along with ferric nitrate and water.

Fe + 3HNO3 → Fe(NO3)3 +3[H] {HNO3 + [H] → NO2 + H2O }× 3 Fe + 6HNO3 → Fe(NO3)3 + 3NO2 + 3H2O With cold and dil. HNO3: Iron reacts with cold and dil. HNO3 to give nitrous oxide along with ferric nitrate and water. {Fe + 3HNO3 → Fe(NO3)3 +3[H]}×8 {2HNO3 + 8[H] → N2O + 5H2O} ×3 8Fe + 30HNO3 → 8Fe(NO3)3 + 3N2O + 15H2O With cold and very dil. HNO3: Iron reacts with very dil. HNO3 to give ammonium nitrate along with ferrous nitrate and water. {Fe + HNO3 → Fe(NO3)2 +2[H]}×4 HNO3 + 8[H] → NH3 + 3H2O NH3 + HNO3 → NH4NO3 4Fe + 10HNO3 → 4Fe(NO3)2 + NH4NO3 + 3H2O Action with less electropositive metals Metals which are less electropositive (like Cu, Bi, Hg, Ag etc) than hydrogen react with nitric acid according to nascent oxygen theory.

HNO3→ NO2+ H2O + [O] conc. HNO3 → NO + H2O + [O] dil. Some examples are: a. HNO3: Copper reacts with conc. nitric acid to give nitrogen dioxide along with cupric nitrate and water. 2HNO3→ 2NO2 +H2O + [O] Cu + [O] → CuO CuO + 2HNO3→ Cu(NO3)2 + H2O Cu+ 4HNO3 → Cu(NO3)2 + 2NO2 + 2H2O With cold and dil. HNO3: Copper reacts with cold and dil. HNO3 to give nitric oxide along with cupric nitrate and water. 2HNO3 → 2NO +H2O + 3 [O] {Cu + [O] → CuO}×3 {CuO + 2HNO3→ Cu(NO3)2 + H2O }×3 Cu+ 8HNO3 → 3Cu(NO3)2 + 2NO + 4H2O
